title: Read a stack trace and logs to find the cause of a timeout (B2)
summary: Read a long set of logs, a stack trace and metrics, trace the failure to its cause and write a short diagnosis.
learningObjectives: Read logs in time order and find the first error
Read a stack trace from the top frame
Write a diagnosis that separates evidence from guesses

parts.heading: Incident summary
parts.content: Synthetic training artifact — non-production. Incident 2291. Report export timeouts. Reported by support at 14:05 UTC. Users who press Export on the monthly report page wait about thirty seconds and then see the message Request timed out. About one in four export requests fails. Other pages are not affected. The evidence below was collected by the on-call engineer: application logs, a stack trace from the worker, database metrics and the recent deploy history. Read the logs in time order first, then the stack trace from the top frame down, and note which facts are observed and which are only guesses.

parts.heading: Application log excerpt
parts.content:
13:58:02 INFO export-service request id=r-501 user=u-77 report=monthly started
13:58:04 INFO export-service request id=r-501 query started table=orders rows=2400000
13:58:34 WARN export-service request id=r-501 slow query 30.0s
13:58:34 ERROR export-service request id=r-501 timeout after 30s
13:59:10 INFO export-service request id=r-502 user=u-12 report=weekly started
13:59:11 INFO export-service request id=r-502 completed rows=51000 time=0.9s
14:01:46 ERROR export-service request id=r-503 timeout after 30s report=monthly

parts.heading: Stack trace from the worker
parts.content:
TimeoutError: query exceeded 30000 ms
    at Pool.query (db/pool.js:88)
    at loadOrders (reports/orders.js:41)
    at buildMonthlyReport (reports/monthly.js:17)
    at handleExport (api/export.js:63)
Caused by: statement timeout on connection 12. The top frame, Pool.query, shows where the error was raised, but the useful clue is the second frame: loadOrders loads every order of the month in one query, with no limit and no filter by date index.

parts.heading: Database metrics
parts.content: Between 13:50 and 14:10 the primary database CPU was between forty and fifty percent, which is normal. Connections in use were 38 of 50, which is higher than the usual 20, because slow exports keep their connections open for thirty seconds. The orders table has 2.4 million rows. The index on created_at exists, but the query in loadOrders sorts by customer name first, so the database cannot use that index. Weekly reports are fast because they read about fifty thousand rows.

parts.heading: Recent deploy history
parts.content: Tuesday 10:12: export-service 4.2.0 released. Change: monthly report now includes customer names, which needs a join with the customers table. Tuesday 16:40: no further changes. Previous release 4.1.3 was on Thursday last week. The first timeout in the logs appears on Tuesday at 10:31, about twenty minutes after the 4.2.0 release. No infrastructure changes were made this week, and the database version is unchanged since March.

parts.heading: Engineer notes
parts.content: Observed: monthly exports time out after thirty seconds; weekly exports are fast; the slow query reads 2.4 million rows; the first timeout appeared after release 4.2.0. Guess: the join with customer names and the sort by name prevent the use of the date index. Not yet checked: the query plan, and whether a smaller date range avoids the problem. Next step: run EXPLAIN on the query and test a version that filters by date first and joins names afterwards.

vocabulary.technicalMeaning: Danh sách các hàm đang chạy khi lỗi xảy ra.
vocabulary.example: The stack trace shows where the error was raised.
vocabulary.commonMistake: Viết stack trace thành hai từ.

vocabulary.technicalMeaning: Yêu cầu bị dừng vì chạy quá lâu.
vocabulary.example: The request timed out after thirty seconds.
vocabulary.commonMistake: Danh từ viết timeout, động từ viết time out.

vocabulary.technicalMeaning: Sự thật có trong log hoặc số liệu.
vocabulary.example: We observed that weekly exports are fast.
vocabulary.commonMistake: Dùng observed cho điều thấy được, không phải điều đoán.

vocabulary.definition: có liên quan về thời gian
vocabulary.technicalMeaning: Hai sự kiện xảy ra cùng lúc nhưng chưa chắc có quan hệ nhân quả.
vocabulary.example: The timeouts correlate with the release.

vocabulary.definition: kế hoạch thực thi truy vấn
vocabulary.technicalMeaning: Cách cơ sở dữ liệu quyết định chạy một truy vấn.
vocabulary.example: We need to check the query plan.
vocabulary.commonMistake: Query plan là cụm cố định hai từ.

expressions.meaning: Nêu điều quan sát từ log.
expressions.example: The logs show that the first timeout appeared at 10:31.

expressions.meaning: Nêu manh mối từ stack trace.
expressions.example: The stack trace points to loadOrders, which loads every order of the month.
This is only a hypothesis: the join blocks the date index.
To confirm this, we should run EXPLAIN on the query.

correctAnswer: The logs show a timeout after thirty seconds.
exercises.explanation: Quan sát dựa vào log, không suy đoán.

Sắp xếp cách đọc bằng chứng.
options: read the logs in time order
read the stack trace from the top
correctAnswer: read the logs in time order
read the stack trace from the top
exercises.explanation: Log, stack trace, tách sự thật khỏi phỏng đoán, bước kiểm tra.

performanceTask.title: Write a short diagnosis
performanceTask.scenario: You read the evidence of an incident and write a short diagnosis for the team.
performanceTask.baselinePrompt: Read the short log and trace excerpt and write a diagnosis in English (60 to 120 words): what you observed, your hypothesis and the next check. Do not look at the model answer yet.
performanceTask.performancePrompt: Write a short diagnosis in English, 60 to 120 words: what the evidence shows, your hypothesis and the next check.
performanceTask.modelResponse: Diagnosis for incident 2291. Observed: monthly report exports time out after thirty seconds, about one in four requests fails, weekly exports are fast, and the first timeout appeared twenty minutes after release 4.2.0. The stack trace points to loadOrders, which reads 2.4 million rows with no limit. Hypothesis: the new join with customer names and the sort by name prevent the use of the created_at index. This is not confirmed yet. Next check: run EXPLAIN on the query and test a version that filters by date before the join.
performanceTask.retryPrompt: Write the diagnosis again in English. Keep the structure and mark guesses more clearly.
performanceTask.transferPrompt: Write a diagnosis for a different failure, using observed facts, a hypothesis and a next check.
performanceTask.reviewPrompt: Write a diagnosis for another failure without looking at old notes.

rubric.label: Facts, hypothesis, next check
rubric.description: The diagnosis separates facts from guesses and ends with a check.

anchors.met: The reader sees observed facts, one hypothesis and a next check.
anchors.notMet: Guesses are written as facts or no next check is given.

rubric.label: Accurate evidence
rubric.description: Times, numbers and names match the evidence.

anchors.met: Numbers and function names are correct.

rubric.label: Cautious language
rubric.description: Uses cautious words for unconfirmed ideas.
